recentItems.title: Rising Chip Prices Push up Phone Prices in China
recentItems.description:
In China, smartphone manufacturers are increasing their prices as the global demand for microchips to power the AI industry disrupts supplies of the essential phone part.

The sales manager at a shop in Huaqiangbei, a renown electronics mall in southern China, says several name brand phone makers have increased their prices this year, sometimes more than once.

The high prices are giving some consumers pause, while others have succumbed to fact that smart phones are essential in today's world.

Experts say over the past year, the global price of storage chips for smart phones has continued to rise. Plus, the costs of components like capacitors have also risen.

Although the overall smart phone market is under pressure, some product categories, like foldable phones, have seen growth.

Data from market research institutions shows that from January to August this year, some 4.5 million homegrown foldable phones were sold.

recentItems.title: Chinese Snacks Satiate Global Palates
recentItems.description:
Chinese exports of things like candy and salty snacks are seeing an increase in demand lately.

At a food company in eastern China’s Quanzhou City, a batch of gummies is filtering through an assembly line, getting prepared for shipment overseas.

The company says overseas markets now account for 70 percent of their total sales. Part of their success, the company director says, is due to their differentiated products, based on client preferences.

Quanzhou is now home to 378 casual snack export enterprises.

Customs data shows that food companies in the city exported 318 million U.S. dollars-worth of snacks in the first seven months of the year.

recentItems.title: LIVE: China holds ceremony to commemorate the 95th anniversary of September 18 Incident
recentItems.description:
Today marks the 95th anniversary of the September 18 Incident. On September 18, 1931, Japanese troops blew up a section of the South Manchurian railway under their control in Shenyang, capital of northeast China's Liaoning Province and blamed China for the sabotage. They used it as a pretext for invasion of Shenyang and then the whole region. The incident marked the beginning of the 14 years of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and opened up the prelude to the world's anti-fascist war.

recentItems.title: LIVE: What Is the WorldSkills Competition All About?
recentItems.description:
The highly anticipated 48th WorldSkills Competition is about to take place in Shanghai. Skills competitors from around the world will gather along the Huangpu River, pursuing their dreams through craftsmanship and showcasing the brilliance of technical skills in the new era.

From September 16 to 18, Audrey will take you on an exploration of the WorldSkills Museum—the only museum in the world dedicated to skills. Here you will learn about the century-long history of the WorldSkills Competition. Together with Serbian video blogger Filip, you will experience the craftsmanship behind China’s intangible cultural heritage, and join Iraqi video blogger Al Kalthoom Aya in trying out WorldSkills competition disciplines.

Tune in to the livestream and discover the beauty of skills.
